title: InATheGer - Model project for intensified interprofessional outpatient therapy for geriatric patients
summary:
In old age, several illnesses often occur simultaneously and the frequency of health restrictions and frailty increases. A good 20 per cent of women and over ten per cent of men in the 75 to 79 age group are already considered physically frail. In Germany, there are currently no structured, outpatient, local treatment concepts available for this age group. They are particularly needed in rural areas simply because of the long journeys involved. The InATheGer project team has set itself the goal of improving outpatient care for older patients through a standardised interprofessional treatment offering. The GP-led concept bundles outpatient, GP-led treatment and counselling services close to home in one centre with the involvement of non-physician healthcare professions. The aim is to bundle and coordinate patient-orientated services and to enable access for patients with limited mobility. The close and coordinated interprofessional cooperation is intended to support GPs in the outpatient care of frail patients. 
The suitability of the concept will be tested at the same time. A total of over 500 elderly and frail people from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern will be invited to take part in the study. Half of these will be randomly selected to take part in the therapy programme. The concept includes individually tailored treatment with remedies, nutritional counselling and adjustments to visual aids and hearing aids. A total of 50 therapy units (spread over 20 days) are administered over 14 weeks. All participants are surveyed at study inclusion and after 18 and 31 weeks after study inclusion, regardless of their participation in the therapy programme.  Their need for support with tasks of daily living, assessment of their own quality of life, characteristics that indicate frailty, number of hospital admissions and medication intake are examined. Conclusions about the effects of the programme will be drawn from the comparison.
conditions: Geriatric patients with clinical deterioration diagnosed by a family doctor (acute or progressive in the last year)

interventions.name: Participants in the intervention group receive the new form of care InATheGer in addition to statutory standard care: an intensive, multimodal, outpatient therapy programme tailored to geriatric patients. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Able and willing to give consent
Age ≥70 years
AND at least 2 of the following criteria:
- Degree of care
- Mobility impairment
- Frailty
- Chronic pain syndrome
- Cognitive and emotional impairment
AND (acute clinical deterioration in the last 6 months OR progressive clinical deterioration within the last 12 months)
- Member of the statutory health insurance scheme
Exclusion criteria:
- Refusal or inability to participate in the study- Need for inpatient treatment
- Completely bedridden
- Nursing home resident
- Patient is unable to complete a simple questionnaire
- Life expectancy less than 8 months
